title: fr.linagora.twalk.persona.suggest.produced.v1
description: A persona produced a suggested reply for human oversight. Nothing is ever sent on the sole basis of this event: a suggestion only becomes a reply when a persona.reply.approved event references it. Produced by Hermes on the NATS JetStream bus.

specversion.description: CloudEvents specification version. Fixed to 1.0 for all Twalk v1 events.

id.description: Deterministic identifier computed as sha256(persona_id + ':' + trigger_event_id + ':' + attempt), with attempt starting at 1. Several suggestions may exist for the same trigger; each attempt has its own id while remaining replay-safe.

source.description: URI identifying the persona that produced the suggestion. Format: hermes://<domain>/personas/<persona_id>.

type.description: CloudEvents type. Reverse-DNS convention with an explicit version suffix. Any breaking change to this schema requires incrementing the suffix (v2, v3, ...) rather than mutating v1.

time.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of when Hermes produced the event.

subject.description: CloudEvents id of the trigger event the suggestion replies to.

datacontenttype.description: Fixed to application/json for all Twalk v1 events.

dataschema.description: Optional URI pointing back to this JSON Schema. Recommended for third-party consumers that validate events dynamically.

traceparent.description: Optional W3C Trace Context traceparent header, normally continued from the trigger event.

network.description: Twalk extension. Network of the trigger event, copied for server-side filtering on NATS without deserializing the data payload.

connection.description: Twalk extension (ADR 0033). The **connection** this event belongs to — the one configured account the deployment observed it on or acts through — by the id the Companion Gateway's registry gave it. `network` says what kind of thing that is; this says which one. Handed to the producer, never derived by it; see definitions/connection.schema.json.

consent.description: Twalk extension. Consent state of the trigger event's sender, copied from the trigger.

persona_id.description: Identifier of the persona that produced the suggestion.

event_id.description: CloudEvents id of the trigger event. Identical to the top-level subject.

event_type.description: CloudEvents type of the trigger event.

trigger.description: Structured reference to the event the suggestion replies to.

contact.description: Optional. The contact's display name as the trigger carried it (`data.contact.display_name`), so an approval surface can say who is being answered without anyone reopening the message (#160's decision, #334). **Written by this side**, never by an agent: a persona publishing through the SDK has read the message; the Companion Gateway, publishing an answer that came back from Hermes (#360), reads that one member of the trigger and nothing else of its `data` — not the body, not an attachment, not the `network_identifier` beside it, which the contract populates only when consent allows. The name and not the identity, because on a bridged network the identity is a phone number inside a Matrix ID and the screen is read by a human. Absent when the trigger carried none: an approval that says what is asked without saying by whom is worth more than one that says neither, and a name invented from an identity would be an assertion nobody made.

summary.description: What the contact asked, in the persona's own words — never a quotation of their message. Written by the only component allowed to read that message, at the moment it reads it, so that no component downstream has to reopen an inbound event to draw an approval screen (#110, ADR 0012). It is content derived from a contact's message and is governed as such: a surface shows it only while the label the trigger carried is granted. The caps and the prohibitions the SDK enforces — no address, no attachment name, no quotation — are what keeps a model's prose from becoming a second excerpt.

context.description: Optional. Who this reply answers and what they asked, written by the persona at publication time (#334, resolving #160). Never the contact's own words.

body.description: The suggested reply in its canonical text form.

format.description: Content type of the body field. text/plain is the default and safest.

attempt.description: Suggestion number for this trigger, starting at 1. Part of the id natural key.

confidence.description: Optional self-reported confidence of the persona, for oversight display. Not a correctness guarantee.

rationale.description: Optional short explanation of why the persona suggests this reply, for oversight display.

expires_at.description: Optional RFC 3339 timestamp after which the suggestion should be considered stale (e.g. a same-day appointment answer).

disclosure.description: Optional. The sentence disclosing that this reply was drafted with an AI assistant, in the language the persona wrote in (ADR 0019), selected from contracts/disclosure/v1/sentences.json by the only component that knows that language. Never part of the suggestion body itself: the Companion Gateway appends it, at approval, to the body a human can otherwise edit freely (ADR 0031). Its addition to this v1 schema, closed with additionalProperties: false, is a deliberate exception to the new-suffix rule this schema's own type field states, recorded and accepted in ADR 0031.

times.description: Optional. Whether the times this reply names were verified before it was published (#383), and absent when it names none — which is most replies. Written by the publishing side, never by an agent: a value here is an assertion about what was checked, and the component that did the checking is the only one that may make it. The member exists because the two kinds of draft are otherwise indistinguishable on an approval screen. A reply that offers instants in proposed is checked against the windows its agent read and against the owner's calendar, and one that fails is never published at all; but a reply may also name a time in its prose and list nothing, and refusing that on a text pattern would refuse "je te réponds sous 24h", which is not a proposal. So it is published and said to be unverified, and the owner reading it knows which of the two they hold. Added to this v1 schema, closed with additionalProperties: false, on the same reasoning ADR 0031 recorded for disclosure.

state.description: checked: every instant the reply offered was inside a window its agent had read for this message and inside a free gap of the owner's calendar, asked again at the moment of publication. unverified: the reply's text names something time-like and it offered no instants, so nothing here was verified — not a refusal and not a defect, a label.

count.description: How many instants were checked. Present with checked and absent otherwise: there is no count of things that were not counted.
